    Remove duplicates from an iterable while preserving the original order.

    Works for hashable items, such as strings, numbers, tuples, etc.

They form when massive stars collapse under their own gravity after exhausting their nuclear fuel, or through other extreme cosmic processes. At the center of a black hole is a point of extremely dense matter called a **singularity**, where known physics breaks down.

Black holes can be:
- **Stellar-mass**: formed from collapsed stars
- **Supermassive**: millions to billions of times the mass of the Sun, found at galaxy centers
- **Intermediate-mass**: smaller than supermassive but larger than stellar-mass

They are not “cosmic vacuum cleaners.” If the Sun were replaced by a black hole of the same mass, Earth’s orbit would remain essentially the same—though life would be destroyed by the loss of sunlight.

- Every year divisible by **4** is a leap year.
